raw_response:
My name does not matter. I am old now, 63 years, and my hands know this land better than my head knows numbers. Let me tell you how I will do things this year.

I have 12.4 mu. That is not small, not big. My husband and I are two mouths. Our son works in the city in Shijiazhuang, he sends money sometimes but he does not come back to help in the field much. So the work falls on me and some hired hands at busy time.

I will plant cotton on about 2 mu — the piece near the road where the soil is lighter and not so good for wheat. The rest, about 10.4 mu, I do wheat in winter and maize in summer. This is what everyone does here. This is what my neighbors do. I do the same.

For seeds — I buy from the shop in town. They sell me the improved ones. The old village seeds, nobody keeps them anymore. The shop man tells me which one is good this year and I buy what my neighbor Aunt Zhang bought last year because her wheat was thick and heavy.

For fertilizer, I think in bags. One bag is 50 jin — no wait, the compound fertilizer bag is 40 kilo. I count by bags.

**Wheat:** I put about 2 bags of compound fertilizer per mu before planting, then one bag of urea at the spring green-up time. That is maybe 18 kilo nitrogen per mu, 7 kilo phosphate, 6 kilo potash. I water 3 times — once before winter, once at green-up, once when the head comes. My well is good so water is no problem, only the electricity cost. Spray pesticide 2 times, once for aphids, once for rust if I see yellow spots.

**Maize:** After wheat harvest, I plant right away, no plough, just rotary cultivator — that is what the machine man does now. Base fertilizer one and half bag compound, then top-dress one bag urea when maize is knee high. About 16 kilo nitrogen, 6 phosphate, 5 potash. Water 2 times if the summer is dry. Spray 1 time for the borer worm.

**Cotton:** Cotton is more trouble. I put 1.5 bag compound at planting, and some more nitrogen when it starts flowering. About 14 kilo nitrogen. I water 3 times. Cotton needs many sprays for the bollworm — I spray 5 times, sometimes 6. Cotton price is not so good anymore but I keep a small patch, old habit.

I would rather put one extra half-bag than have a thin crop. Fertilizer money I can make back, but if the wheat is yellow and short, the whole year is finished. This is what my mother-in-law taught me and it is still true.

Plough — I do not plough deep anymore. The machine man comes with rotary, cheaper. Only cotton field I plough once in autumn because that land gets hard.
